advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether transient Gerrit transport failures should mark the bot degraded (flapping) vs. only sustained auth rejections, and confirm the added per-poll Gerrit round-trip latency is acceptable for autodeploy/docker probes.
evidence: 541:     auth_ok, auth_reason = await asyncio.to_thread(_gerrit_auth_health, app.state.config)
188:         status = exc.status if exc.status is not None else "transport"
A URLError (transient network) becomes gerrit_auth_failed:transport -> status=degraded, and observability publishes reviewbot_healthy=0
advisory.finding: The /health handler now makes a blocking outbound Gerrit call (up to the 5s timeout) on EVERY poll via asyncio.to_thread(_gerrit_auth_health). autodeploy and docker poll /health frequently, so this adds Gerrit coupling and up-to-5s latency to a previously cheap liveness route, and a transient Gerrit transport blip transitions the bot to status=degraded (publishing reviewbot_healthy=0), which can flap alarms.
scenarios: Gerrit briefly unreachable (as documented in the ticket during host reboots) while the review-bot process is fully healthy
High-frequency health polling adds a 5s-bounded outbound call per poll

advisory.finding: /health now performs a synchronous Gerrit auth network call on every request (check_auth with a 5s socket timeout), but autodeploy's drain probe curls /health with -m INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT (default 5s). When Gerrit is slow/unreachable, /health latency approaches or exceeds 5s, so bot_in_flight_reviews() times out and returns -1 (in_flight unreadable), causing the deploy to run WITHOUT the drain check and kill in-flight reviews — the exact regression the drain contract exists to prevent.
